Maya R: FYI found a weird slot-density migration pattern on the INT8 builds when serving long sessions (~12k tokens). Memory use climbs steadily and we end up paging more aggressively, which correlates with ~7-12% generation latency tail growth. dump from perf job attached below.

InfraBot: perf-job #rwd-perf-942 finished: https://ci.redwood/infer/perf-942 — profile artifacts at s3://redwood-perf/perf-942/kv-profile.pb.gz

Maya R: Short summary: on INT8 with our default slot allocation (slot_size=64b, packing=high) we see slot fragmentation: many partially-filled slots after repeated longctx requests. When the runtime tries to compact it triggers a chain of page evictions which blows up pin counts -> CUDA memory pressure -> kernel fallback that hurts latency.

TJ: Can you paste the line from the timeline that shows eviction vs kernel fallback?

Maya R: Sure — snippet from the timeline (filtered):
```
[00:00:23.140] kv_alloc: +48MB (slots packed)
[00:01:12.993] kv_frag_scan: found 18% partial slots -> schedule compact
[00:01:13.010] scheduler: start_compact job@node-3
[00:01:13.118] kv_evict: evicted 12 pages (3x chained) -> CUDA mem free: -120MB
[00:01:13.220] kernel_select: fallback to bf16-kernel (quant-int8 not available) latency +18ms
[00:01:45.004] restore: repopulate warmpages -> throughput drop until warmup
```

Sasha: Interesting. Do we know whether this is purely fragmentation (slot packing) or also wear-leveling from int8 table layouts? I remember a paper noting int8 per-channel packing can make coalescing harder.

Maya R: Looks like both. The profiling histograms show a bimodal slot occupancy distribution: ~65% either 100% full or <25% occupancy -> lots of tiny holes that compaction doesn't merge efficiently because of the alignment constraints of our int8 pages (32B boundary).

Liam: Could be kernel selection heuristics too: our choose_kernel() currently prefers the int8 path if any page is quantized; but once eviction touches a mixed page we flip to fallback. Maybe we should bias to keep int8 only when contiguous pages > threshold. Quick heuristic: require >80% contiguous quantized density in a page frame to use int8-kernel.

Danielle: Short-term mitigation: we rolled a canary yesterday that forces periodic aggressive compaction during low-rps windows, plus a tiny bump to eviction_threshold (0.65->0.72). Early results: memory climb flattened and end-to-end p95 improved ~4% on canary. No accuracy change observed yet in auto-evals. :thumbsup:

PerfBot: regression-check: 2475009999/canary -> p95_latency delta -4.1%, token-cost delta +0.2%, accuracy-regressions none (on evalset small-conversational-v2).

TJ: Good. Do we have a repro that QA can run locally (one-liner)?

Maya R: Yes — run this on a dev GPU node with model xlm-large-int8 and session script:
```
# repro longctx fragmentation
python perf/repro/longctx_stream.py --model xlm-large-int8 --session-len 12000 --rps 8 --duration 15m --pack-mode high
```

Sasha: For medium-term: propose two fixes in parallel:
1) Kernel heuristic: add contiguous-quantized-density threshold before selecting int8 kernel (Liam idea).
2) Slot allocator: consider variable slot sizes (micro-splitting big slots into 2/4 smaller ones if occupancy drops below 40% for N epochs). This reduces fragmentation but increases metadata overhead — need telemetry.

Liam: Agreed. Also add an opt-in flag for 'prefer-stable-kernel' so Dedicated customers can opt to never flip kernels mid-session.

Danielle: Can someone file an RFC-ish PR with measured tradeoffs? Include: memory savings vs eval-accuracy delta by quant-mode, compaction cpu cost, and impact on batching latency. I'll prioritize review.

Maya R: I'll draft a short doc and attach the perf histograms (slot occupancy, page-churn, kernel-switch events). TL;DR: INT8 saves ~38% peak GPU memory on average, but with longctx churn we see a 6-10% p95 latency risk unless we tighten compaction/allocator heuristics.

TJ: Thanks — @Maya R can you add the exact test vectors you used for the accuracy checks? Want to confirm it's not just small-convos bias.

Maya R: Yep will add the eval set and the run commands. Also plan to spin a small ablation: int8 w/ micro-split allocator vs int8 w/ heuristic-only vs bf16 baseline. Schedule for tomorrow.

InfraBot: Created ticket INF-3812 "slot-density migration: int8 fragmentation mitigation" and linked perf artifacts.

Danielle: Nice, let's keep it lightweight — if the micro-split gains <3% p95 improvement it's not worth added complexity. For now canary config looks safe to ramp to 10% traffic.

Maya R: Good plan. Will post back with ablation numbers. Thanks all.
